examples.scenario: EA +/-15cm RMSE is published as a guaranteed maximum cell error.
examples.reason: RMSE is a dataset-level error statistic, not a deterministic per-cell bound.

examples.scenario: EA DTM and DSM share the same RMSE so they are treated as equivalent terrain sources.
examples.reason: Surface semantics remain different even when nominal accuracy metadata matches.

examples.scenario: A 25cm and a 2m DTM are assigned identical local uncertainty solely because both say +/-15cm RMSE.
examples.reason: Resolution and processing lineage are separate from dataset RMSE.

examples.scenario: Survey-period transformation metadata is omitted from an uncertainty report.
examples.reason: EA states transformation/geoidal model can depend on survey period.

examples.scenario: NVA and VVA are collapsed into one universal parcel error value.
examples.reason: USGS assesses nonvegetated and vegetated vertical accuracy separately.

examples.scenario: VVA 95th percentile is converted to RMSE without a distribution model.
examples.reason: Percentile and RMSE metrics are not interchangeable without justified assumptions.

examples.scenario: Old 95% confidence reporting is mixed with current ASPRS 2024 thresholds.
examples.reason: USGS documents a change in current reporting methodology.

examples.scenario: Checkpoint survey error is added again to a current USGS RMSEv value that already includes it.
examples.reason: Current USGS methodology specifies inclusion of survey error in NVA RMSEv.

examples.scenario: High pulse density is used to claim lower vertical RMSE than the project metadata.
examples.reason: USGS states density alone does not upgrade the vertical accuracy quality level.

examples.scenario: Swath overlap RMSDv is reported as absolute DEM accuracy.
examples.reason: Relative/internal precision and absolute vertical accuracy are distinct metrics.

examples.scenario: Standard deviation is labelled accuracy with no bias term.
examples.reason: USGS notes standard deviation does not account for systematic error.

examples.scenario: OSGM15 0.008m is reported as total parcel-height uncertainty.
examples.reason: OSGM15 model error excludes GNSS and does not include DTM or sampling error.

examples.scenario: OSGM15 mainland error is applied to a different regional datum.
examples.reason: OS publishes different standard errors by regional height datum.

examples.scenario: OSGM15 absolute error and local relative error are treated as the same quantity.
examples.reason: OS separately describes absolute model error and much smaller local relative error.

examples.scenario: A four-hour GNSS example accuracy is used for every target with no GNSS observation metadata.
examples.reason: GNSS height accuracy depends on observation method, hardware and environment.

examples.scenario: EPSG:7711 accuracy metadata is presented as measured target terrain accuracy.
examples.reason: Transformation metadata is not parcel-specific DTM validation.

examples.scenario: Stored raster integer precision is treated as the same thing as physical elevation accuracy.
examples.reason: Scale/offset and survey accuracy are separate concepts.

examples.scenario: Float32 output is assumed exact because no explicit rounding was coded.
examples.reason: Finite numeric representation remains an auditable precision component.

examples.scenario: NODATA cells are assigned a very large uncertainty and retained in extrema.
examples.reason: NODATA is invalid data, not a valid elevation with uncertainty.

examples.scenario: Bilinearly resampled DTM cells are marked as native observations.
examples.reason: Derived interpolation lineage must remain explicit.

examples.scenario: A filled void value receives the same uncertainty label as native terrain.
examples.reason: Void interpolation is a distinct derived-data treatment.

examples.scenario: Below-bridge interpolated terrain receives no treatment flag.
examples.reason: Derived below-bridge terrain must be auditable separately from native ground.

examples.scenario: Hydroflattened water cells are assigned ordinary land-terrain uncertainty.
examples.reason: Hydroflattening is a specialized surface treatment.

examples.scenario: A cell just outside the parcel is selected after boundary perturbation but uncertainty ledger ignores membership sensitivity.
examples.reason: Membership changes can change extrema identity, not merely value precision.

examples.scenario: Half-pixel address drift chooses a neighboring cell but only vertical RMSE is reported.
examples.reason: Spatial addressing errors can dominate the selected elevation.

examples.scenario: Different source windows return different extrema but window provenance is omitted.
examples.reason: Window identity is part of the uncertainty/reproducibility ledger.

examples.scenario: A CRS transform candidate changes but only final coordinates are compared.
examples.reason: Operation identity and its uncertainty metadata must remain explicit.

examples.scenario: Vertical datum error is added twice: once as OSGM15 and once as EPSG:7711 accuracy.
examples.reason: Those may describe the same transformation model basis.

examples.scenario: Minimum and maximum cell errors are assumed independent and multiplied by sqrt(2).
examples.reason: Both extrema may share correlated survey, datum and processing errors.

examples.scenario: Minimum and maximum errors are assumed perfectly correlated with no evidence.
examples.reason: Correlation structure must be justified rather than chosen for a smaller result.

examples.scenario: Shared vertical datum bias is separately added to both ends of a height difference without covariance analysis.
examples.reason: Common systematic components may partly cancel in a difference.

examples.scenario: Independent local interpolation errors are assumed to cancel.
examples.reason: Only demonstrated shared components can be treated as correlated.

examples.scenario: All uncertainty components are root-sum-squared despite known correlation.
examples.reason: RSS assumes an appropriate independence/covariance model.

examples.scenario: All uncertainty components are added linearly and called one-sigma uncertainty.
examples.reason: Combination method and statistical meaning must be explicit.

examples.scenario: Bias and random uncertainty are merged before documenting each source.
examples.reason: Systematic and random components behave differently under differencing and averaging.

examples.scenario: Survey-wide RMSE is interpreted as the exact uncertainty at one steep parcel.
examples.reason: Parcel-specific terrain, land cover and treatment context remain relevant.

examples.scenario: Nearest checkpoint residual is copied as the parcel cell error.
examples.reason: A checkpoint is an independent validation sample, not the exact target-cell error.

examples.scenario: Parcel vegetation status is unknown but VVA/NVA choice is made anyway.
examples.reason: Metric selection requires applicable land-cover context.

examples.scenario: Parcel source survey ID is unknown but a survey-specific RMSE is assigned.
examples.reason: Uncertainty components must be tied to the actual contributing source.

examples.scenario: Parcel resolution is inferred from a product family name rather than runtime raster metadata.
examples.reason: Exact target raster identity is required.

examples.scenario: Water, bridge, void and resampling flags are absent but a numeric parcel uncertainty is emitted.
examples.reason: Treatment-specific uncertainty cannot be assessed without those flags.

examples.scenario: Two uncertainty ledgers have the same total but different components.
examples.reason: Same aggregate number does not prove reproducible provenance.

examples.scenario: Primary and independent component totals differ slightly and are averaged.
examples.reason: Independent replay mismatch must be resolved, not averaged away.

examples.scenario: Component values use metres and centimetres without explicit normalization.
examples.reason: All components must be transformed to a common unit before combination.

examples.scenario: An uncertainty component has no source citation or derivation.
examples.reason: Every component requires traceable evidence or explicit runtime derivation.

examples.scenario: A component uses a normal-distribution conversion with no distribution assumption recorded.
examples.reason: Confidence conversions depend on distribution assumptions.

examples.scenario: A current ASPRS metric is converted using a legacy 95% factor after the standard changed.
examples.reason: Current reporting basis must match the pinned standard version.

examples.scenario: Static uncertainty preparation is complete and parcel-specific uncertainty is written anyway.
examples.reason: Target-specific components require actual canonical execution.

examples.scenario: Canonical point is absent but location-specific OSGM15 regional error is selected.
examples.reason: Target location is required for regional model selection.

examples.scenario: Exact parcel boundary is absent but extrema covariance is calculated from fixture cells.
examples.reason: Actual extrema cells must come from canonical membership execution.

examples.scenario: Known ACK blocker is relabelled pending.
examples.reason: Known unresolved execution conditions remain BLOCKED and pending stays zero.

examples.scenario: A second uncertainty runner is launched while the shared runner ACK is absent.
examples.reason: Continuation contract allows only the existing shared runner.

examples.scenario: 99.99 source-chain readiness is displayed as parcel uncertainty accuracy.
examples.reason: Readiness is preparation confidence, not measured target accuracy.

examples.scenario: Batch 84 is reported as final parcel uncertainty and height-difference output.
examples.reason: Canonical point, exact boundary, runtime DTM and executed extrema are still required.
